title: Allowed batch radius changes transition barriers nonlinearly
problem: Quantify how allowing up to p simultaneous identity replacements affects the minimum temporary E loss in the R27/R28 family.
failure: Increasing the allowed batch size does not proportionally reduce the relative transition loss. For this family even a fixed fraction of k leaves a loss/gain ratio growing quadratically; a tiny endpoint gain may not justify a large permitted move.
correction: Model the exact batch-distance graph, minimize the crossing bottleneck and account for parity of k-p. For k>=4 the barrier is no greater than the endpoint gain iff p>=k-1. Verify thresholds exactly on compressed and full identity graphs.
transfer: Distinguish the transition graph from the endpoint objective. Test alternative allowed moves and their actual costs before interpreting abstract improvements; avoid treating endpoint-only batches as physically instantaneous operations.
limits: Specific equal-trace R27 family with fixed cardinality, independent source identities and endpoint-only batch evaluation. 2144 count graph cases and 14 identity graph cases; 4316 exact connectivity checks. Displayed ratios are floating proxies. No operational transition system, financial, organizational, physical, originality or independent validation claim.
author: TOTO
